title: Predictive Provisioner: tenant-aware smoothing and headroom for embedding throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Embeddings endpoints experience rapid tail-latency spikes and suboptimal cost when many tenants burst concurrently. Current autoscaler reacts to queue length or GPU utilization after the fact, causing scale-up delay and transient throttling. We need a tenant-aware predictive provisioning layer that smooths request admission, creates short-term headroom per-tenant, and pre-provisions capacity based on lightweight demand forecasts so P95/P99 latency improves without large cost increases.
acceptance_criteria: P95 embedding request latency for small models remains < 60ms under steady median load
Scale-up time to handle a 2x sudden tenant burst is < 30s without resetting existing warm caches
Queue tail (99th percentile queue wait) reduced by >= 40% compared to baseline under mixed-tenant workloads
No single-tenant fair-share policy causes more than 5% increase in total infra spend relative to existing autoscaling baseline
All changes are behind a runtime feature flag and can be rolled back in < 5 minutes
technical_approach: Implement a lightweight predictive-provisioner service that runs alongside the embedding router. It ingests 1-minute time-series of per-tenant QPS and token-length histograms, computes an exponentially weighted forecast, and emits a requested headroom token budget per tenant. Router admission controller applies a time-decayed credit pool (elastic headroom) and a token-leaky-bucket shaped dequeue algorithm. Provisioner emits capacity hints to the autoscaler so GPU pools can pre-warm fractional slots. Caches (prefix/KV) are pinned when forecasted headroom > threshold to avoid cold-start cost.
tradeoffs: Forecasting introduces complexity and small risk of over-provisioning; we limit forecast horizon to 60s and cap prewarm capacity to control cost
Per-tenant shaping can increase latency for noisy low-priority tenants; we mitigate with configurable SLAs and emergency bypass for high-tier customers
Adding a control plane component increases operational surface area; will reuse existing auth and metrics collectors to reduce onboarding work
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Read-only prototype - produce forecasts and simulate routing decisions in a staging router; no changes to autoscaler or router behavior
Phase 2: Admission-controller integration - apply elastic headroom credits in router and measure latency/queue impact behind a feature flag
Phase 3: Autoscaler hints - have provisioner send prewarm hints (fractional slot requests) to the autoscaler; ensure evictable warm pools
Phase 4: Gradual rollout - start with low-risk tenants and dedicated dev load; expand by traffic percentile
Data retention: store minute-level aggregates for 72 hours for forecasting and debugging; purge raw request traces after 30 days
rollout_plan: Canary on 5 internal tenants for 48 hours with feature flag ENABLE_PREDICTIVE_PROVISIONER
If latency and cost KPIs hold, open to 25% production traffic by week 2
Full release controlled by runtime flag and rollout policy (A/B + comparison against baseline) with automatic rollback on SLA violations
Post-release runbook: re-enable old admission path by toggling feature flag and notify on-call SRE
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: forecast_bias_abs > 0.4 for 5 minutes => investigate skewed tenant behavior
Alert: scale_up_time > 45s after provisioner hint => autoscaler integration regression
SLO dashboards: per-tenant P95/P99 latency, queue_wait_ms percentiles, prewarm_success_rate
Cost dashboard: incremental infra spend vs baseline (7d moving average)
